data.name: Virginia
data.gender_notes: Virginia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Latin 'Virginalis', meaning 'maiden, virgin'. In Christianity, it refers to the Blessed Virgin Mary, who was born without original sin. The name Virginia carries the meaning “Virgin, pure” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Virginia usually hope their child will grow to embody virgin, pure and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Virginia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Virgin, pure.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Virginia total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
data.cultural_impact: The name Virginia has a rich history and cultural significance, as it is named after the Roman goddess Virtus, meaning virtue, and Queen Virginia of England, who was known for her purity and chastity. In Virginia, USA, the name has been borne by 12 governors, adding to the esteemed reputation of the name. It was also the name of Pocahontas's daughter, symbolizing the blending of two cultures through love and respect.
data.spiritual_significance: Beyond its cultural significance, the name Virginia carries a profound spiritual meaning, as it is derived from the Latin word 'Virginalis', meaning 'maiden, virgin'. In Christianity, it is a nod to the Blessed Virgin Mary, who is celebrated for her purity and holiness. Her virginity is a shining example of self-control, obedience, and loyalty to God. By carrying the name Virginia, one can be reminded of the sacredness of life and the importance of purity and virtue, instilled in us by Mary, the mother of God.
